capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extraction and the batch shape that generate()
accepts: input_features is a fixed 30s (3000-frame) log-mel per call, and
generate(features, prompts) takes a stacked (N, mel, 3000) feature batch
with one prompt list per window.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor(audio) call hard-truncates each recording to
30 seconds — anything past the first window is never fed to the model, so
the dominant error is deletion of the entire tail, not a decode-quality
problem. Batching N stacked 30s windows through one generate() call returns
N independent result objects, one per window.
hypothesis:
Slicing the waveform into consecutive non-overlapping 30s windows and
batch-decoding all of them recovers the deleted tail; concatenating the
per-window decodes should sharply raise length_ratio and cut deletion-driven
CER versus the single-window stub.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs. GPU memory: how many stacked (mel, 3000)
windows one generate() call can hold before CUDA OOMs.
what_i_learned:
Batching ALL 30s windows of a full 0715 call-center recording into one
generate() call exceeds float16 CUDA memory and crashes (RuntimeError: CUDA
out of memory) — the recordings are long enough (many minutes) that the
window count blows the batch. Memory scales with batch size, so decoding one
window per generate() call bounds peak memory to a single window and still
recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Replace the single stacked batched generate() with a sequential loop that
decodes each consecutive 30s window in its own generate() call and joins the
per-window text, eliminating the OOM while preserving long-form coverage.

capability_investigated:
The input side of the pipeline rather than a decode knob — the raw waveform
passed to transcribe() before it reaches processor(). I derived per-frame RMS
energy (20ms frames) on the numpy audio to locate speech vs. silence, an
input the pipeline had never conditioned on. The audio profiles confirm the
signal is there: silence_ratio 6–25% and single silences up to 34s per file.
what_i_learned:
Fixed 30s windowing has two deletion sources independent of decode quality:
seams land mid-utterance (token loss at every boundary), and any window
carrying a long silence feeds that silence to the decoder, which is what
drives Whisper's repetition/hallucination collapse (repeated_text 0.36 on
best). Frame-energy VAD is computable with numpy alone (no silero/backend
dependency) and lets seams fall in silence while clear silence is dropped
from what the model ever sees.
hypothesis:
Replace blind fixed windows with energy-VAD windows: compute frame RMS,
threshold at peak−40dB, merge speech across <0.5s gaps, pad 0.25s, and pack
regions into <=30s windows that break only at silence (force-splitting any
single region longer than 30s). Cutting at silence removes boundary deletions
and feeding less silence should cut the repetition collapse that deletes
whole-window content — directly attacking the coverage/deletion axis while
keeping one-window peak memory.
